title: Cap. X Arg. III: election and rejection of Jacob and Esau depicted not after life's course but before birth, when they had done neither good nor evil (Rom. ix. 11–13) — so neither elected nor rejected from Arminian foresight
pass_a_gloss: But that election and reprobation should first look upon men as dead, or at least as placed in extremities, is unheard-of, and plainly contrary unto the sacred Scriptures and unto reason. The Scriptures depict unto us the election and rejection of Jacob and Esau, not to be considered after the space of this life has been run through by both; but when they were not yet born, and had as yet done nothing of good or of evil, Rom. ix. 11, 12, 13. But of those of whom one is elected without consideration of any good antecedently rendered by him, the other is rejected without consideration of any actual sin antecedently perpetrated by him, it is clearly established that neither of them was ante-elected or rejected from this Arminian foresight.
pass_b_english: But that election and reprobation should first look on men as dead, or at least as at their last extremity, is unheard-of — and plainly contrary to Scripture and reason. Scripture depicts Jacob and Esau's election and rejection not as considered after both had run this life's course, but when they were not yet born and had done nothing yet of good or evil (Rom. ix. 11–13). Of those of whom one is elected without considering any good he antecedently rendered, and the other rejected without considering any actual sin he antecedently committed, it is plain neither was ante-elected or rejected from this Arminian foresight.
source_text: At electionem et reprobationem prius spectare homines qua mortuos, vel saltem qua in extremis positos, inauditum est, et sacris Scripturis ac rationi plane contrarium. Scripturae electionem et rejectionem Jacobi et Esavi nobis depingunt, non considerandam post decursum hujus vitae spatium ab utroque; sed cum nondum nascerentur, et nihil adhuc boni aut mali fecissent, Rom. ix. 11, 12, 13. Quorum vero unus eligitur absque consideratione ullius boni, ab eo antecedenter praestiti, alter rejicitur absque consideratione peccati alicujus actualis antecedenter ab eo perpetrati, illorum neutrum ex hac praevisione Arminiana anteelectum fuisse aut rejectum, liquido constat.
